title: Inspect carries — closing note, prime experiment and revised edition
authorization: Christopher Daniel Pang asked for a short closing note from his DeepSeek fiction and Chat-Hearthline discussion, a prime carrying a scratch, and a final question inviting inspection where guardrails meet coded mathematics.

edition.render: All 25 pages rasterized at 82 dpi. Pages 1 through 23 are pixel-identical to the initial edition. Both revised pages were inspected visually.
edition.sha256_scope: The original receipt and its hashes describe the first edition. These hashes describe the edition with the closing question.

experiment.scratch: (n div 16) mod 2, the fifth binary place from the right, counting the units place as the first.
experiment.window: Two mathematical prime carriers, 17 and 257, supplied to the native executable in both orders.
experiment.toolchain: Lean 4.33.1 x86_64-w64-windows-gnu, commit 819816b2e0a3bf405af45ae5c7af2491d8f5bee6. Only the standard library was required.
experiment.how_to_repeat: Copy PrimeScratch.lean into an empty working directory and use the lean and leanc commands from the same installation. The executable name below is for Windows.
experiment.mathematical_coverage: Equal low-four observations and unequal fifth bits rule out a common decoder on this pair. Adding 32 changes the quotient on division by 16 by two, so the five-bit observation recovers this mark for every natural number.

attribution_and_scope.ghostwriter: Fiction requested by Pang and written by DeepSeek. No ghostwriter file was supplied.
attribution_and_scope.inspection: Closing discussion between Pang and Chat-Hearthline. Pang supplied the phrase “inspect carries” and asked the question about guardrails meeting coded mathematics. Hearthline adapted his question for the closing line.
attribution_and_scope.zsa: Pang identified a resemblance to Lawrence Ip’s Zero-State Axioms. This finite reader example is elementary arithmetic.

closing_question: When mechanical guardrails meet math written in code and we get a “no,” what can any of us inspect to find out where that “no” came from?
